episode.subject: giant sequoia
episode.title: The wrong trunk
episode.body: A cone fell from me onto the path. The man beneath it looked up and complained to the tree beside me. I was enjoying the mistake until he stroked her bark to apologize.

visibleScene: A person leans against an enormous sequoia trunk with arms embracing its bark. Several other trunks are visible beyond it; dry forest floor and woody debris surround the base. The contact is unambiguous. No cone drop, apology, complaint or narrator identification is documented.
imageFit: Foreground embraced sequoia is fictional neighbor, not narrator. This composition shows the affection that reverses his pleasure in the mistaken accusation. First-person prose can illustrate the other participant in the incident; narrator need not occupy foreground.
proseReason: The precise reversal from enjoying misplaced blame to envying the apology is economical and legible. Cone and complaint set up the invented episode; photographed embrace supplies the consequential change. No rewrite needed.
